tips.title: Tu or vous tells you the audience
tips.body: An advert using **tu** imperatives — *découvre*, *essaie*, *n'attends plus* — is aimed at **young people**. **Vous** forms mean adults or the public. It is the quickest evidence for *à qui s'adresse cette publicité ?*, and it is evidence rather than a guess.

tips.title: À partir de means from, not exactly
tips.body: *À partir de 9 euros* means the **cheapest** item is 9 euros, not that everything is. *Livraison gratuite à partir de 20 euros* means free **once you spend 20 or more**. It is the most frequently tested phrase in this topic, and both uses set a minimum.

tips.title: The tu imperative of -er verbs loses its s
tips.body: *Tu achètes* becomes **Achète !** and *tu regardes* becomes **Regarde !** Only **-er** verbs do this; *tu finis* stays **Finis !** Adverts are full of these, so the rule is worth two seconds of checking.

tips.title: Say what it does, not what it says
tips.body: Summarising an advert caps your marks. Describing its **effect** lifts them: **jouer sur**, **laisser entendre que**, **mettre en avant**, and above all **en + present participle** — *en fixant une date, elle crée un sentiment d'urgence*.

steps.title: À quoi sert une publicité
steps.body:
A **publicité**, often shortened to **une pub**, is an advert. Reading questions use them because they pack persuasion into very few words, and every word is doing a job.

An advert almost always has four parts, and naming them helps you answer questions about it.

- **le produit** — what is being sold
- **le public visé** — the target audience
- **le message** — what it claims
- **le but** — the aim: to persuade you to buy, to try, or to change something

The question *Quel est le but de cette publicité ?* is asking for the **aim**, not for a summary. The answer is usually a verb: *persuader les jeunes d'acheter …*, *encourager les gens à recycler …*.

Note the prepositions, which differ and are tested: **persuader quelqu'un ***de*** faire** something, but **encourager quelqu'un ***à*** faire** something.

steps.title: L'impératif
steps.body:
Adverts give orders. That means the **imperative**, and for regular **-er** verbs there is one rule that catches most students out.

Take the **present tense** form and drop the subject pronoun. For **tu** with an **-er** verb, also **drop the s**.

- *tu achètes* → **Achète !** — Buy!
- *nous achetons* → **Achetons !** — Let's buy!
- *vous achetez* → **Achetez !** — Buy! (polite or plural)

So the *tu* imperative of an *-er* verb ends in **-e**, never *-es*. Verbs that are not *-er* keep their s: *tu finis* → **Finis !**

Adverts use **vous** for the public and **tu** for young people, which is itself a clue about the **public visé**. A poster saying *Découvre notre nouveau jeu !* is aimed at teenagers; *Découvrez notre nouvelle gamme* is aimed at adults.

Three irregulars worth knowing because adverts love them: *être* → **Sois !**, *avoir* → **Aie !**, *aller* → **Va !**

steps.title: Le langage de la persuasion
steps.body:
Adverts use a small, repeated set of persuasive words. Recognising them is most of the reading skill.

**Superlatives** — claiming to be the best:

- *le meilleur* — the best
- *le plus grand choix* — the widest choice
- *le numéro un* — number one

**Urgency** — making you act now:

- *offre limitée* — limited offer
- *jusqu'à dimanche* — until Sunday
- *dernière chance* — last chance
- *dépêchez-vous* — hurry up

**Value** — making it feel cheap:

- *gratuit* — free of charge
- *une réduction de 20%* — 20% off
- *moitié prix* — half price
- *à partir de 9 euros* — from 9 euros

That last one is worth pausing on. **À partir de** means **from**, so *à partir de 9 euros* tells you the **cheapest** item costs 9 euros, not that everything does. A reading question will ask whether *tout coûte 9 euros*, and the answer is **non**.

steps.title: Lire une publicité
steps.body:
Here is a short advert of the kind a reading paper uses. Work through it in the order the questions will come.

> **VÉLOMAX** — *Découvre le vélo électrique qui change tout. À partir de 799 euros, livraison gratuite jusqu'à dimanche. N'attends plus : rejoins les 50 000 cyclistes qui ont déjà choisi Vélomax !*

**Le message** : *c'est le meilleur, beaucoup de gens l'ont déjà acheté*
**Le but** : *persuader les jeunes **d'**acheter un vélo électrique*
**Le prix** : *à partir de 799 euros* means the **cheapest** model is 799 euros
**L'urgence** : *jusqu'à dimanche* — free delivery ends Sunday, which is what makes you hurry

steps.title: Ce que la publicité ne dit pas
steps.body:
The higher-mark questions ask you to be **critical**, not to summarise. Useful phrases:

- **la publicité exagère** — the advert exaggerates
- **ce n'est pas très honnête** — it isn't very honest
- **on ne sait pas si c'est vrai** — we don't know if it's true
- **ça donne envie d'acheter** — it makes you want to buy
- **la publicité cache le vrai prix** — the advert hides the real price
- **elle joue sur les émotions** — it plays on emotions

> *À mon avis, cette publicité **exagère**, car elle dit que le produit **change tout**, ce qui est impossible.*

Two things to look for when you are asked what an advert is hiding.

- **À partir de** hides the **top** price. Only the cheapest model costs that.
- A **deadline** such as *jusqu'à dimanche* creates urgency that has nothing to do with whether the product is good.

**Donner envie de** is a very useful structure: *ça donne envie **d'**acheter* — it makes you want to buy. It always takes **de** before the infinitive.

steps.title: À toi : analyse cette publicité
steps.body:
> **ÉCOSAC** — *Essayez nos sacs réutilisables ! Le meilleur choix pour la planète. À partir de 3 euros, livraison gratuite à partir de 20 euros d'achat. Offre limitée jusqu'au 30 avril.*

**Partie A.** Réponds en français, en phrases complètes.

1. Quel est le produit ?
2. À qui s'adresse cette publicité, à ton avis ? Justifie ta réponse.
3. Quel est le but de cette publicité ?

**Partie B.**

4. Combien coûte le sac le moins cher ?
5. Est-ce que la livraison est toujours gratuite ? Explique.
6. Trouve deux techniques de persuasion et nomme-les.

**Partie C.** Écris trois phrases donnant ton opinion sur cette publicité. Est-elle honnête ? Est-ce qu'elle te donne envie d'acheter ? Pourquoi ?

Question 5 is the trap: read *à partir de 20 euros d'achat* carefully.

steps.title: Aller plus loin: décrire l'effet, pas le contenu
steps.body:
The difference between a middle and a top answer on an advert is the difference between saying **what it says** and saying **what it does to you**.

> *La publicité dit que le sac est bon pour la planète.* — content.
> *La publicité **joue sur** le sentiment de culpabilité : en disant que c'est « le meilleur choix pour la planète », elle **laisse entendre** que les autres clients ne s'en soucient pas.* — effect.

The second uses two structures worth learning:

- **jouer sur** — to play on (a feeling)
- **laisser entendre que** — to imply that

And two more for the same job:

- **faire croire que** — to make you believe that
- **mettre en avant** — to highlight, to push forward

> *Elle **met en avant** le prix bas et **fait croire que** c'est une bonne affaire.*

**A structure worth having ready**: *en* + present participle, meaning *by doing something*.

> ***En disant** « offre limitée », la publicité crée un sentiment d'urgence.* — By saying "limited offer", the advert creates a sense of urgency.

The present participle is formed from the *nous* form of the present, minus **-ons**, plus **-ant**: *nous disons* → *disant*, *nous faisons* → *faisant*, *nous utilisons* → *utilisant*. Three irregulars: *être* → **étant**, *avoir* → **ayant**, *savoir* → **sachant**.

That structure alone will lift an answer, because very few candidates use it and it reads as genuinely analytical rather than descriptive.

steps.title: Résumé
steps.body:
- Identify four things in any advert: **le produit**, **le public visé**, **le message**, **le but**.
- **Le but** is answered with a **verb**: *persuader … **d'**acheter*, *encourager … **à** recycler*. Note the different prepositions.
- The **imperative** of an **-er** verb loses the **s** in the *tu* form: *Achète !*, *Découvre !*
- An advert using **tu** is aimed at **young people**; **vous** at adults or the public.
- Persuasion comes in three kinds: **superlatives** (*le meilleur*), **urgency** (*offre limitée*, *dernière chance*) and **value** (*gratuit*, *moitié prix*).
- **À partir de** means **from**: it gives the **lowest** price, or a **minimum condition**. It is the most commonly tested phrase in this topic.
- To criticise: *la publicité exagère*, *ce n'est pas honnête*, *on ne sait pas si c'est vrai*, *ça donne envie **de** …*
- For top marks, describe the **effect**, not the content: **jouer sur**, **laisser entendre que**, **faire croire que**, **mettre en avant**.
- **En + present participle** means *by doing*: *en disant*, *en montrant*, *en fixant*.
- Form it from the *nous* present minus **-ons** plus **-ant**. Irregulars: **étant**, **ayant**, **sachant**.

questions.modelAnswer:
**Modèle.**

> *Cette publicité vend des sacs réutilisables. Elle **s'adresse** probablement **aux adultes**, parce qu'elle utilise le **vouvoiement**, avec l'impératif *essayez*. Le but est de **persuader** les gens **d'**acheter ces sacs, **en jouant sur** leur envie de protéger la planète. Elle utilise aussi **l'urgence**, car l'offre est limitée jusqu'au 30 avril, **ce qui pousse** les clients à acheter tout de suite. À mon avis, elle n'est pas complètement honnête, parce qu'**à partir de** trois euros **laisse entendre que** tous les sacs sont bon marché, alors qu'on ne connaît pas le prix des autres.*

**What earns the marks.** The audience is justified from the **vouvoiement**, not asserted. *Persuader **de***, with the right preposition. **En jouant sur** — *en* plus a present participle. And the opinion turns on the actual wording, *à partir de*, rather than on a general feeling.

questions.solution: Discover our new range! From 15 euros, with free delivery until Sunday. Don't wait any longer: join the 20,000 customers who already trust us.

criteria.text: Renders the imperatives correctly as English imperatives
Renders *à partir de* as 'from' and *jusqu'à* as 'until'

questions.modelAnswer:
**Traduction.**

> **Discover** our new range! **From** 15 euros, with **free delivery until Sunday**. **Don't wait any longer**: **join** the 20,000 customers **who already trust us**.

**Three things to notice.**

- *Découvre*, *n'attends*, *rejoins* are **tu imperatives** — the advert is aimed at young people, and they become plain English imperatives.
- ***À partir de*** is **from**, not *starting at exactly*. And *jusqu'à dimanche* is **until Sunday**, a deadline.
- ***Faire confiance à quelqu'un*** is **to trust someone**, so *qui nous font confiance* is *who trust us* — not *who make us confidence*.

examTechnique.body:
Read the advert twice: once for what it sells, once for how it is trying to persuade you.

For the audience, look at **tu** or **vous** and quote it. An answer with evidence scores above one with an assertion.

For the aim, use a verb: *persuader … d'acheter*, *encourager … à essayer*. Check the preposition, because the two verbs differ.

Watch **à partir de** every time it appears. It sets a **minimum**, whether of price or of spending, and questions are built on candidates missing that.

When asked for an opinion, judge the advert's **honesty** and point at the wording that makes you say so. A general feeling is worth less than a quotation.

For the highest marks, describe what the advert **does** — plays on a feeling, implies something, creates urgency — and reach for *en* plus a present participle at least once.
examinerErrors: Reading *à partir de 9 euros* as 'everything costs 9 euros'.
Writing *Achètes !* with an s; the tu imperative of an -er verb drops it.
Saying who the advert targets without quoting the tu or vous form that proves it.
Using *persuader à* or *encourager de*; it is persuader **de** and encourager **à**.
Summarising what the advert says when asked what it does.
Translating *faire confiance à* literally instead of as 'to trust'.
Forming the present participle from the infinitive rather than from the nous form.
Giving an opinion on the product rather than on the advert.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A top answer treats the advert as something constructed and says how it was built. It names the target audience and quotes the pronoun that proves it, reads *à partir de* correctly wherever it appears, and separates the claim from the evidence for the claim. Asked for an opinion, it judges the advert rather than the product, and it points at the exact phrase that is doing the persuading. It uses the analytical verbs — *jouer sur*, *laisser entendre*, *mettre en avant* — and at least one *en* plus present participle, which very few candidates attempt and which reads as genuine analysis rather than description.
